usage: All the students were happy after they passed the test.
hint: Use 'all' when you mean 'every single one' of something.
Use 'any' when you don't care which specific thing is being referred to.

usage: The weather today is feeling really bad.
hint: Think of something that isn't enjoyable or isn't working well.

usage: The tree is big and strong.
hint: Think of something that takes up a lot of space!

usage: The night sky is black with stars.
hint: Think of something that absorbs light, like a dark room.

definition: A color like the sky or a deep ocean.
usage: The dress was blue and looked beautiful.
hint: Think of something calm and peaceful.

usage: The morning sky was bright and sunny.
hint: Think of something that shines or glows.

definition: Having a lot of things to do
usage: The kids were busy building a tower.
hint: Think of something that keeps you from being bored.
Think of something that lets light pass through easily.

usage: The box was closed, so I couldn't open it.
hint: Think of something that is not open or accessible.
Think of something that isn't hot, like ice or a winter day.

definition: very difficult or challenging to understand
usage: The robot's programming is complex, but it can solve many problems.
hint: Use this word when something is so hard to grasp that it feels like a mystery.
